![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/11b85e35604a0350a9fd7754dfda481000debb20397d9aa593a1b887409a97c7.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}$ and $y=2x,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}$ and $g(x)=2x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2} & =2x \\ 8x-{x}^{3}-2x & =0 \\ 4x-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ x(4-{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ x(2-x)(2+x)\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-2,$ $x=0,$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2$ because we are only concerned about $x\ge 0.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/e03c88c1d24116cc9f68c69150eba39cb6593b4bf6fd4ca9640987ce4ba62299.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=2x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x([4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}]-[2x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(2x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
